The defendant Ng Sui-ting appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts and a black face mask. The charges allege that the defendant on 10 July and 17 August respectively allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog, without being restrained by a leash not exceeding two metres in length, to enter the area around YOHO Mall in Yuen Long, and is charged with two counts of "allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place".

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks before the next mention, and did not oppose bail. Acting Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for "allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place" carries a fine of HK$25,000 and imprisonment for three months.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) Yip Yin said yesterday that if the dog owner decides to hand the large dog over to the government, the department would consider methods including humane euthanasia; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the animal may be classified as a "known dangerous dog", and the court may order that the dog must wear a muzzle whenever it goes out in future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection organisation Mochi Rescue (毛守救援), told Collective (《集誌社》) that the dog owner has regretted signing the abandonment form; he also said Mochi Rescue is willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer for rehabilitation.
